_doc: Database Contract Sentinel configuration.
Three sections, three different meanings. They are deliberately NOT one list,
because 'static analysis cannot prove this' and 'this is broken and we know it'
are different claims with different lifetimes.
tables         -- permanent exceptions. The reference is CORRECT but cannot be
proven correct by static analysis. Every entry must say what
it is, who owns it, and why it is unprovable. An anonymous
permanent exception is how a gate stops meaning anything.
known_defects  -- the reference is WRONG and the fix is a separate commit.
This exists so the sentinel can land green on a repo that
already has defects, without pretending they are acceptable.
Entries carry the evidence that they are real. This list is
expected to shrink to empty and never grow.
retired_objects-- objects that were REMOVED and must never come back. Any
runtime reference to one is a hard failure regardless of
whether something later re-declares it.

_doc: The message-privacy defect is CLOSED. These names were the defect.
private_chat_blocks never existed: no CREATE TABLE, no migration, no writer,
no production row. A SELECT against it inside a bare except made a block
check a permanent no-op that still read correctly in source review.
users.message_privacy and users.dm_privacy are columns that were never added
to the users table. Enforcement lives in blocked_users plus the comm_v2
block stores.
IMPORTANT -- this is matched structurally, against resolved table references
from an AST walk, NOT against file text. bot.py contains the string
'private_chat_blocks' today inside an explanatory comment about the fix. A
text-matching guard would report a closed defect as open.

tables.name: private_chat_blocks
tables.why_fatal: It never existed. Any runtime read of it is a security check that cannot fire.
